the development of multiporphyrins on cyclotri-phosphazene scaffold, which is an important step toward the design and synthesis of multiporphyrine arrays for potential applications in the fields of molecular electronics, photonic devices, and molecular recognition.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the noncovalent assembly of porphyrin on cyclotriosphosphazene scaffold is a simple and convenient approach for the construction of multiporphyrins.
cyclotriphospha-zenes can be considered as versatile platforms for the synthesis of multiporphyrins and multipyridyls.
the noncovalent approach is a better choice for the assembly of multiporphyrins than the covalent approach, as the former is a better mimic of natural photosynthetic systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyclotriphosphate scaffold is a suitable platform for the assembly of porphyrin macrocycles with different porphyrin numbers.
the cyclotriphosazene scaffold can be a versatile platform for the synthesis of multiporphyrins in a controlled manner.
the noncovalent approach can be used to prepare multiporphyrin arrays with a high yield.
